I need to replace my hot water heater and am not quite sure if I should go tankless or not. My house is just under 900SF, and right now it's just two people living here. The cost seems to be about the same for either where I'm looking, but I'm not sure what benefits might be for one over the other; we don't use a ton of hot water and we're not generally running hot water for multiple purposes at once (shower & laundry at same time) etc.

This is a first for me as a homeowner so help/input is so greatly appreciated.
Dont go tankless. They are not as reliable. Also with a tank you always have a nice reserve of water in the case of an emergency. Always think of things from all angles.
Seconded. I’ve had both and the tankless was fickle and was a bitch to service

Tankless units (also called “on demand” units) heat water only when you turn on the faucet. They usually operate on natural gas or propane. The main advantage is that they eliminate the extra cost of keeping 40 to 50 gallons of water hot in a storage tank, so you waste less energy.

Some say tankless last a lot longer than typical water heaters if properly maintained. If your local government doesn't require a tankless water and this is not your forever home, get the standard.

In my experience tankless water heaters cost up to 3 times as much as your standard water heater.
To reiterate get the standard unless you are investing in your home because you are living there for the rest of your life.

From what I remember when I was looking a few years ago is new tank water heaters are so well insulated that they use virtually no gas/electricity keeping the water hot. The tankless use a lot of energy to heat water when being used, but zero while not. There wasn’t much advantage with either with regards to energy. The tankless are much less reliable. Could have changed one way or another in the last couple years.
Tankless also need to be serviced yearly. So they cost more to buy and, after you include servicing, they probably aren't saving you a lot of money to run either.

Go with a regular 40gal. Around here they cost +/- 325$CAD. Change it every 8-10 years even if it is still working great. Drain the tank every 3-4 years to remove the shit at the bottom. Don't put it directly on concrete (I use 2inch foam board). If you live in a hot climate, add a layer of insulation around the tank. Let me know if you need more info. I own rental properties and changed probably 25-30 tanks in the past...

My wife really, really wants a tankless since it never runs out of hot water. I don't want it because I know that my costs will skyrocket since some folks around here don't seem to get out of the shower until there is no hot water left (ie: my 20 year old daughter). But truthfully, it is going to depend on your needs. If your current one was providing for your needs and your costs were not unreasonable I would go standard. Matter of fact, standard is probably the best for most people and especially in a house that small with only 2 people.

I think the tankless things can come with an extra shutoff just for that though, i.e. a timer or something.

But you should really get your kid into taking 8 minute showers. I have waist length hair and mine are maybe 12 minutes? I only wash my hair every 3-4 days though(if you shampoo/condition daily it will get really frizzy because you are stripping the hair too much), so my daily shower might be 5 mins.?

The most efficient thing to do is if you have the traditional water heater - turn the power off ( at the circuit box ) everyday ! I would turn mine on for about 10 minutes before I took a shower and turn it off right after the shower !! You can not believe how much electricity it saves ! A girl from FPL told me to do this years ago. If you have to just put up a note in your bathroom to turn it on in the morning - no reason to keep on heating the water in the tank if no one is using it. Good Luck !

If you tank is really large, 10 minutes is probably not enough to get the water hot enough for a comfortable shower; you will have to turn the water all the way to hot.

Also, it is important for the water to stay above 60°C to prevent the growth of bacteria and other disease-causing germs…
You can always do both and have a tank that is set to a lower temp like 65°C and put the tankless heater in line to ramp up the temperature as needed during use.
Just be careful not to go much lower than that.

It depends on how the mineral content is in your water supply.
